A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VCoT-Lift framework and VCoT-Bench study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and matchable, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark-construction statistics and experiments evaluating ten LLMs across proof-removal ratios, types, and locations, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds pipeline model-selection experiments, semantic-judge comparisons and bias measurements, and Best-of-10 results.

M1.justification: The transformer–checker loop, proof-rule hierarchy, abstraction filtering, pruning, repair, and benchmark-construction procedures remain unchanged. Appendix B.2 newly identifies the models implementing pipeline stages; v1 provides no corresponding assignments establishing an actual method change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 150 Verus-Bench programs and 1,988 completion tasks, with the same Ratio, Type, and Location coverage. The added analyses reuse this material; different sampling budgets and a 20-program ablation subset do not introduce new coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds three-model pipeline comparisons and an eight-candidate semantic-judge comparison, substantially expanding evaluated alternatives. Table 3 also replaces the reported Gemini 3 checkpoint with Gemini 3.1 Pro. Unchanged scores and retained Gemini 3 plot legends leave unclear whether that replacement reflects rerunning or correcting model identification.

E3.justification: v2 adds Best-of-10 evaluation, a three-model ablation on 20 randomly sampled programs using lifted proof lines and repair rounds, and expanded judge validation with within-family versus other-family false-positive measurements. These are substantial new protocols on existing coverage. Newly specified decoding limits do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New analyses test pipeline model selection, semantic-judge reliability and family bias, and robustness to multiple generation attempts (Appendices B.2 and D). Section 4.2 also adds inspection of failed Qwen thinking traces, identifying predicate drift and hallucinated lemmas. These materially extend v1's diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: The new Best-of-10 experiment reports a ten-attempt budget, adding repeated-attempt information. These attempts support best-of selection rather than uncertainty estimation; neither version reports seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 adds pipeline-selection results, judge accuracy and bias tables, and Best-of-10 scores, including 46.92% assertion accuracy for Claude Sonnet 4.5 and 52.50% Middle accuracy for Gemini 3 Flash. The unnamed judge's 94% agreement report becomes an expanded comparison selecting GPT-5 mini at 92.7%, not a demonstrated same-setting decline. Tables 1, 4, and 5 retain their numerical values despite the Gemini identity revision.

T1.justification: Appendix D.1 introduces the mathematical definition Self-Bias = FPR(Own) - FPR(Other). Otherwise, the weighted accuracy equation, Z3 rule semantics, and example verification reasoning are unchanged; no new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction narrow the evaluation framing from whether models truly understand verification to whether they can systematically reconstruct its explicit deductive steps. The four principal contributions and the headline finding of fragile verification reasoning remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 extends the semantic-drift explanation with cascading errors in thinking traces, interprets judge family bias and sampling limitations, and adds specific curriculum, proof-type-aware training, and intermediate-reward recommendations in Section 5. These refine and extend the existing interpretation of reliance on local proof scaffolding.

D1.justification: v2 identifies pipeline-stage models and the final semantic judge, specifies temperature settings and a 32,768-token output limit, and reports construction, model-evaluation, and judge costs. It also adds an artifact-repository address. These substantially expand reproducibility information; the hardware description was already present in v1.

R1.justification: The Gemini 3 source is replaced with a Gemini 3.1 Pro reference. Positioning against prior verification and proof-hint-generation work remains unchanged. The CodePlan publication-detail correction refers to the same work and does not constitute an additional research citation.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized terminology, grammar, and numbering corrections, adds a Discussion section, acknowledgments and an impact statement, and extends the appendix organization. Most existing paragraphs and the main method-and-results narrative are retained rather than extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: Tables 6–8 and Figure 11 substantially expand the visual presentation with a judge-comparison matrix, family-bias measurements, and Best-of-10 results. Table 3 gains a cost column, and several existing displays are relocated or rearranged. The original methodological diagrams and benchmark plots are retained.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's unnamed judge and sparse implementation disclosure, v2 improves transparency and adds useful checks of judge reliability, pipeline choices, and repeated-attempt performance. The gain is limited by unreconciled Gemini checkpoint labels alongside unchanged scores, and by Best-of-10 sampling settings that remain unclear alongside the stated temperature-zero setup. These issues constrain the strength and reproducibility of the added evidence.
